models_evaluated: 15 open-weights LLMs (4B-120B), including medically fine-tuned 4B and 27B variants

links.outcome: Robust representation of neurological terms across model size, fine-tuning and complexity
links.effect: Robustness followed log-linear scaling with size (r=0.736); fine-tuning gave no benefit at 4B but raised 27B from 38.2% to 62.6%; most models degraded sharply with rising term complexity.
links.quote: While representational robustness broadly follows model size scaling laws, neither model size nor fine-tuning guarantees clinical reliability.

unlisted_practices: Validating representational robustness of locally deployable LLMs for specific use cases and terminology subdomains
Use of a semantic complexity index to assess term difficulty

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating the robustness of medical term representations across 15 open-weight LLMs across model sizes and fine-tuning states.
